summits_covered.name: Tamil Nadu Global Investors Meet (GIM) 2024 - flagship edition
Samsung Electronics bilateral MoU signing with Government of Tamil Nadu
CM Stalin UAE investment roadshow (Lulu Group MoU)
Pou Chen / High Glory Footwear India bilateral MoU signing with Government of Tamil Nadu

method: WebSearch to identify candidate MoU announcements from Guidance Tamil Nadu (state investment promotion agency), Tamil Nadu Global Investors Meet 2024 official/press coverage, Singapore MTI press materials, and reputable Indian business press (Business Today, Deccan Herald, Business Standard, Swarajya, The News Minute, Entrepreneur India, EVreporter, The Print). WebFetch used to open and read each candidate source rather than relying on search snippets. Wikipedia pages for individual foreign companies (VinFast, Pegatron, Hyundai Motor India, First Solar, Sembcorp) were fetched as a secondary check for real-world follow-through status. Only individually named foreign (non-India-headquartered) companies with a dated, sourced MoU are recorded as verified entries; aggregate summit-total figures (e.g. '631 MoUs worth Rs 6.64 lakh crore' at GIM 2024) are deliberately NOT used as data points themselves and are flagged in negative_notes as classic MoU-graveyard-risk press figures. Web search quota was exhausted mid-sweep; remaining verification relied on WebFetch against already-identified URLs and Wikipedia, so several promising leads (Foxconn housing investment, Delta Electronics, Crocs, Evervan Kothari, ANSR) could not be independently confirmed and were left out or moved to negative_notes rather than reported as verified.

mous.proposed_investment: Up to USD 2 billion total planned (Rs ~16,000 crore); USD 500 million committed for Phase 1 over 5 years
mous.notes: 400-acre facility in Thoothukudi, designed for up to 150,000 vehicles/year. Groundbreaking February 2024; inaugurated by CM M.K. Stalin on 2025-08-04, currently running CKD (completely-knocked-down) assembly with an initial capacity of ~50,000 units/year. Battery manufacturing had not yet commenced as of the check date. This is a genuine, verified follow-through case, not just a press-release total.

mous.sector: Electric vehicles / smart mobility / hydrogen research (with IIT-Madras)
mous.proposed_investment: Rs 6,180 crore (reported elsewhere as Rs 6,200 crore); additional Rs 20,000 crore over 10 years cited in some coverage
mous.notes: Hyundai already operates an existing 850,000-vehicle/year plant at Irungattukottai, Tamil Nadu (pre-dating this MoU). This 2024 MoU is for EV/battery expansion plus a hydrogen research centre; no independent confirmation of the expansion's construction status was found in this sweep.

Pegatron's existing India plant was already producing iPhones prior to this MoU. Ownership changed materially afterward: Tata Group acquired a 60% stake in Pegatron's India unit in January 2025 (per Wikipedia), so the facility is now majority Indian-owned even though the original MoU signatory was the Taiwanese parent.
MoU was for a Chennai design centre targeting ~1,600 jobs. No independent confirmation of the centre opening or hiring progress was found in this sweep.
Wikipedia's First Solar manufacturing-facilities list confirms a Tamil Nadu, India factory was commissioned in 2024, consistent with the GIM 2024 MoU actually converting to a real operating plant.
Named as 'Mitsubishi' in secondary press roundups without specifying which Mitsubishi group entity (Electric, Corporation, Heavy Industries, etc.) signed. Left as reported pending clearer sourcing.

mous.proposed_investment: Amount not specified in available sources
mous.notes: Named in a GIM 2024 roundup without a stated investment figure or sector detail beyond 'transport & logistics'.

mous.sector: Energy / infrastructure (exact sub-sector not specified in sources found)
mous.notes: This is one of the largest single figures attributed to any company at GIM 2024. Sembcorp's own Wikipedia India section (checked as a cross-reference) does not currently mention a Tamil Nadu project, which is a caution flag for MoU-graveyard risk on a headline-sized commitment; treat the investment figure as a proposed/announced number only, not a confirmed spend.

Would be Hi-P's first manufacturing plant in India, targeting ~700 jobs. Signed in the presence of CM M.K. Stalin and Singapore Minister S. Iswaran. No independent construction/operational update found in this sweep.

mous.summit_or_event: Bilateral MoU signing with Government of Tamil Nadu
mous.notes: 22-acre plant in Sriperumbudur with 8-million-unit/year capacity. A later Deccan Herald headline ('Samsung to expand its Tamil Nadu plant with Rs 1,000 crore') implies the original plant became operational and was subsequently expanded, but the full article body could not be retrieved (403 error) to confirm details directly, so this status rests on the headline plus general Samsung India reporting rather than a fully read source.

mous.company: Pou Chen Corporation (via India subsidiary High Glory Footwear India)
mous.sector: Non-leather footwear manufacturing (contract manufacturer for Nike, Adidas)
mous.summit_or_event: Bilateral MoU signing with Government of Tamil Nadu
mous.notes: Unit to be set up in SIPCOT Industrial Park, Ulundurpettai, Kallakurichi district; targeting 20,000 jobs over 12 years. No independent confirmation of construction progress or plant opening found in this sweep.

mous.sector: Retail (shopping malls) and food processing / export
mous.proposed_investment: Rs 3,500 crore (Rs 2,500 crore for two malls, Rs 1,000 crore for a food-processing unit)
mous.notes: At signing, a Coimbatore hypermarket was targeted for end-2022 and a Chennai mall for 2024. This sweep could not independently re-confirm opening dates before the web-search quota ran out; treat as unconfirmed rather than assume completion.

mous.company: Bosch Global Software Technologies (Indian arm of Robert Bosch GmbH)
mous.country_of_headquarters: Germany (parent Robert Bosch GmbH; signatory is its India-registered software subsidiary)
mous.sector: Cybersecurity / AI Centre of Excellence (with TIDCO)
mous.notes: Signed only 12 days before this sweep's cutoff, so no follow-through news would be expected yet. Flagged as LOW confidence primarily because the signing entity is an Indian-registered subsidiary rather than the German parent directly — included because the ultimate HQ (Robert Bosch GmbH) is genuinely foreign, but this is a borderline case for a 'foreign company MoU' classification and should be reviewed.

negative_notes: Aggregate summit totals were deliberately excluded as data points: GIM 2024 press claimed 631 MoUs worth Rs 6.64 lakh crore (~USD 80 billion, ~2.69 million jobs); a separate 'Investment Conclave' claimed 104 MoUs worth Rs 1.02 lakh crore; a July 2022 event claimed 60 MoUs worth Rs 1.25 lakh crore; a Coimbatore Investors' Conclave claimed 59 MoUs worth Rs 34,000 crore. These are the classic 'MoU graveyard' headline figures this sweep was designed to look past — only individually named, sourced foreign companies from within these totals were extracted into the mous list above.

Daimler India Commercial Vehicles (Germany, via Daimler Truck) — Rs 2,277 crore Oragadam plant-expansion MoU — found and well-sourced, but dated to May 2020, which falls outside the 2021-2026 window specified for this sweep. Excluded on date grounds only.

Salcomp PLC (Finland) — Rs 1,300 crore expansion of its Nokia Telecom SEZ facility in Sriperumbudur — sources gave conflicting dates (one ties it to the 2019 GIM, another to a May 2020 batch of 17 foreign-investor MoUs). Could not pin down a date inside the 2021-2026 window with confidence, so excluded.

The 'Tamil Nadu signs MoUs with 17 foreign investors' batch (Rs 15,218 crore, companies from France, Taiwan, Japan, China, including IGL Transplantation Solutions and Vivid Solaire Energy) is dated May 2020 — just before this sweep's window — and was excluded on date grounds, not for lack of verifiability.

Feng Tay Group (Taiwan) — operates a large existing footwear manufacturing presence in Tamil Nadu (Lotus, East Wind, Fairway units in Cheyyar/Bargur, reportedly ~40,000 workers) — but the only dated MoU/announcement material found in this sweep is from 2006 (original MoU) and a 2020 announcement of two more factories, both outside the 2021-2026 window. A fresh Feng Tay MoU within the window may exist but was not found/verified here.

Foxconn / Hon Hai — a ~Rs 706 crore worker-housing/residential-complex investment was referenced in a secondary source (via a synthesized theprint.in summary) as occurring around August 2024, but the original article could not be located and read directly, so neither the exact date nor whether it constitutes a formal state MoU (versus a company-internal capex decision) could be confirmed. Excluded pending direct-source verification. Foxconn's large pre-existing Sriperumbudur mobile-assembly campus is real and operational but its founding MoU predates this window.

Delta Electronics (Taiwan) — referenced in the same secondary source as employing ~20,000 in Tamil Nadu electronics manufacturing, but no MoU date or investment figure was found; excluded pending verification.

Crocs — appeared only as a Deccan Herald headline ('Crocs footwear to be manufactured in Tamil Nadu') found via search snippet; the article body was never opened due to WebSearch quota exhaustion, so company nationality confirmation, investment figure, sector detail, and date are all unverified. Excluded.

Evervan Kothari — referenced in a Deccan Herald headline (Rs 5,000 crore non-leather footwear units in Karur/Perambalur) found only via snippet; the 'Kothari' component of the name suggests a joint venture with an Indian partner, and foreign-HQ status could not be confirmed. Excluded.

ANSR — signed a GCC (Global Capability Centre) facilitation MoU with Guidance Tamil Nadu in November 2025, but ANSR's headquarters appears to be dual US (Austin, Texas)/India (Bengaluru), and this sweep could not clearly establish it as a foreign-headquartered company for this dataset's purposes. Excluded pending verification.

The Vettri Tamil Nadu Investors' Conclave (2026-08-13) source also reported 'seven institutional MoUs...with companies and organisations from Kazakhstan, New Zealand and Russia' without naming the specific entities. Excluded because no individual company names were available in the source read.

Singapore Investment Conclave (2023-05-25) also produced MoUs with Singapore Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries, Singapore University of Technology and Design, and Singapore-India Partnership Office (multiple, with SIPCOT/FaMe TN/TANSIM) — these are institutional/academic/government-to-government cooperation MoUs, not individually named foreign company investments, so they were excluded from the mous list even though they are genuine and dated.

WebSearch quota (200 calls/session) was exhausted partway through this sweep. Remaining research relied on WebFetch against already-known URLs, Wikipedia, and Bing search-result pages (which returned only generic listings, not usable detail). This means several plausible additional TN foreign-MoU candidates from 2021-2026 almost certainly exist but were not found in this pass — this list should be treated as a verified subset, not an exhaustive one.
